findings.reason: it fixes the node's scope to one change in the command group and tells the node the measurement that proves it, instead of a per-library whack-a-mole that the report would have to rediscover.
findings.text: the endpoint is blocked by one eager call, `register_commands()`, which at import time imports all fifteen command modules (`imas_codex/cli/__init__.py:61-75`); measured, §2's target command `imas_codex.cli.serve` costs 8 ms and `imas_codex.cli.discover` costs 28.8 s of a 30 s import, so the design the brief should carry is lazy resolution in the existing group (`click.Group.get_command` / a deferred command table) so that no command module is imported until its name is invoked, with the full command list in `--help` still produced from the table — not a per-module deferral of `litellm` inside `serve`

findings.reason: a node that reaches for a new deferral while this one sits unused at the wrong point in the sequence builds the parallel mechanism the plan's own rubric warns about.
findings.text: a deferred-import mechanism for exactly this problem already exists and is defeated by the site above: `_warmup` starts one background thread per heavy group precisely so the server "complete its stdio handshake … while the slow imports proceed in parallel", and `warmup.start()` runs at `imas_codex/llm/server.py:83` — which is reached only from inside `serve()` at `imas_codex/cli/serve.py:110`, i.e. after the eager group registration has already burned 20-30 s on the same imports synchronously; the endpoint must be stated against this mechanism (start the deferral before the group resolves, or make the group lazy so warmup is not racing a cost already paid)

findings.reason: these are the named parts §2's 90 % attribution rule already requires the node to account for; naming them in the brief saves the node the profiling pass, but the endpoint does not change.
findings.text: census of the eager-import sites on the serve path that the lazy-group change must leave alone but the record must account for: `imas_codex/graph/__init__.py:26` runs `ensure_models_fresh()` and `:55` imports `graph.schema` (+`linkml_runtime`, 5.1 s) and `graph.models` at package import; `imas_codex/cli/discover/sequence.py` → `imas_codex/discovery/base/services.py` → `imas_codex/discovery/base/facility.py` reach that package; and `imas_codex/discovery/paths/scorer.py` imports `litellm` (21.5 s)

findings.reason: the negative control is the only mechanical thing that can distinguish the deep change from a special-case wrapper, and as written it cannot.
findings.text: the guard §2 specifies ("a test fails when starting the server imports the language-model client library") is narrower than the endpoint in a way that lets a wrong design pass: `litellm` is imported by a *sibling* command module (`discovery/paths/scorer.py` via `cli/discover`), never by the serve path, so a design that special-cases `serve` — a `--fast` flag, a conditional import in `serve.py`, a second entry point — passes the guard and still crosses the client limit, because the handshake cost the plan is fixing is the group registration, not one library; the guard should be asserted at the boundary the client sees (no heavy group imported when `imas-codex --help` exits and when the protocol's `initialize` is answered), over the whole heavy set rather than one library

findings.reason: the node brief should extend these two files; two parallel harnesses would drift, and the tool enumerator reads a private registry attribute that only one owner should track.
findings.text: census of existing harnesses the §2 checks would re-implement: `_run_fresh_interpreter` (`tests/discovery/test_engine_import_order.py:12-21`) already spawns a fresh interpreter with `PYTHONPATH` set and asserts on `sys.modules`, in a module whose docstring is "Import order checks for discovery engines and CLI registration" — this is the owner of an import-boundary guard, and a serve-startup guard belongs beside it (or in a helper it exports) rather than as a second subprocess harness; and the tool-list parity check §2 requires has an owner too — `tests/llm/test_tool_schemas.py:20-25` `_tool_names()` walks the server's registered tool components and is driven by an `AgentsServer(dd_only=True)` fixture (`:31-34`) that needs no Neo4j

findings.reason: it changes how the evidence script is written, not what the endpoint claims; the plan already fixes the quantity, tolerance and control.
findings.text: a second-order duplicate the brief must close: the startup record §2 asks for (spawn as `.mcp.json` does, time to first `initialize`) has no owner anywhere in `scripts/` or `tests/`, and `.mcp.json` is the one place a spawn recipe is also encoded — the design should take the spawn recipe from the committed `.mcp.json` (`uv run --no-sync --project … imas-codex serve`) rather than hand-copying the argv into an evidence script, so a change to the configuration cannot silently diverge from the timings the plan cites

response_events.note: §2's guard is now stated at the boundary the client sees: no discovery, language-model client or schema-runtime package is imported before initialize is answered; the lazy command table is the brief's method

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the endpoint is one deep change inside the command group, but §2's guard pins a single library import rather than the handshake boundary, so a shallow per-module deferral would satisfy it while the dominant cost survives.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the new fresh-interpreter import guard and the tool-list parity check each duplicate a harness that already exists in tests.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds no CLI option, no MCP view and no refusal family, and requires the tool list to be identical by name in all three serve modes.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the codebase already owns a deferred-import mechanism (`imas_codex/llm/_warmup.py`) and one eagerly-importing command group defeats it; the design must extend those, not add a third deferral path.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 adds no layer over existing machinery; it changes what an existing entry point costs before it exists.
